title: Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained. Issue 1 (timeliness of complaint against censure): yes. Issue 2 (SJC appellate review of LAP's exercise of original jurisdiction): yes. Issue 3 (LAP erred in finding contumacy): yes. Relief: LAP's judgment, for lack of jurisdiction, is a nullity; Mike Holland is subject to Delhi Presbyterian Church Session and its decisions. Three dissents (Donahoe, Duncan, Harrell); vote 18 concurring, 3 dissenting, 2 absent.
first_summary: The SJC reversed Louisiana Presbytery's judgment finding Mike Holland guilty of contumacy, because the Delhi session had investigated and did not refuse to act under BCO 33-1, so the presbytery's assumption of original jurisdiction was invalid. The court held the complaint timely and the jurisdictional issue reviewable. Three commissioners dissented.
summary: The SJC sustained a session's timely complaint that Louisiana Presbytery barred one of its members from the Lord's Table after assuming original jurisdiction. Under BCO 33-1, a presbytery may assume jurisdiction only when the session 'refuses to act'; because the session had investigated and found no strong presumption of guilt, it acted, so LAP never acquired jurisdiction. The censure was therefore a nullity, and the member remained under his session. The SJC also held the jurisdictional assumption reviewable despite no timely complaint against it. Three commissioners dissented.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Canonical case ID/title at line 1; SJC, 32nd Assembly (2004), printed pp. 78-103; adopted by the full SJC on October 17, 2003, vote 18 concurring, 3 dissenting, 2 absent (line 247).
evidence_notes.dispute: Delhi Presbyterian Church Session complained that Louisiana Presbytery, after assuming original jurisdiction over member Mike Holland, indicted and convicted him of contumacy and barred him from the Lord's Table; DPC asserted LAP lacked jurisdiction because DPC had investigated and concluded no process was warranted (lines 17-123).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered all three issues yes, sustained the complaint, declared LAP's judgment a nullity for lack of jurisdiction, and left Holland subject to DPC Session. Decisive reason: DPC's investigation and no-strong-presumption finding was 'action' under BCO 33-1, so LAP had no basis to assume original jurisdiction; jurisdictional boundaries are constitutionally preset and reviewable through the timely complaint against the censure (lines 125-239).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted majority reasoning is distinct from three dissents (Donahoe, Duncan, Harrell), which dispute reviewability, the 'refuses to act' interpretation, and disposition; vote 18 concur, 3 dissent, 2 absent (lines 243-247, 249-719).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Dissents cite Abshire v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery, 2002-11, and Tampa 2000 Judicial Matter 99-1 (TE Wood) (M28GA pp. 238-241, 310; M29GA pp. 70-82); these are not majority-adopted results (lines 404-424, 527-539, 675-685).

source_limits: The source is the SJC report with majority and dissenting opinions, not the full Record of the Case, briefs, transcripts, or independent copies of the cited Abshire/Tampa matters. Quoted incorporated decisions appear only in the dissenting opinions.
